label: Final copy step of length-3 sequences (t=5)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely (91% of mass) on the last step of L=3 sequences (t=5, input = orig(1) fed back, outputting orig(2)); it is active on ~91% of such steps. Never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter step. The remaining ~9% of mass is weak, scattered activity near the end of the copy phase in longer sequences (mostly L=6-9, t=11-14 and t=17 for L=9), generally under 0.3 of max. Strongest activations (top quartile, ~100% covered) are L=3 t=5 with input tokens such as v/u/d/b; it does not fire on the last copy step of other lengths (to_go==0 alone gives precision 0.03).

issues: Minor numeric slip: the explanation says to_go==0 alone has precision 0.03, but on the test split it is 0.014 (recall 0.85, F1 0.028). This makes the point stronger, not weaker.

The other ~10% of activation mass (1007 test steps) is spread thinly over the end of the copy phase in L=6-9 and t=17 for L=9. Each of those cells has an active rate of about 1% or less. Adding (L==9)&(t==17) drops F1 to 0.225, and adding (to_go<=1)&(L>=6) drops it to 0.023. So no cheap extension recovers it, and it is not a systematic class the predicate should cover.
The 228 test false positives (L=3, t=5 steps where the unit is silent) show no obvious token pattern in the sampled examples, which look like ordinary length-3 sequences.

Provenance problem outside this verdict: the user asked to run the baseline on features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5 (the 1/5 subsample), but this analysis used features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store, and nobody checked that this store was built from the subsample.
